Team / Amelia,

Please find attached a tracked redline of the MSA T4C clause (ACME_MSA_redline_v1.docx) and a short internal playbook (redwood_t4t_termination_playbook_v1.docx). High level notes:

1) Clause language (high level):
- Standard: either party may terminate for convenience with a 60-day written notice. Customer termination during a prepaid commitment results in pro rata credit of prepayments for unused term, minus any committed-discount true-up if the initial pricing was contingent on a multi-year discount.
- Optional concession: Customer may elect 30-day notice in exchange for an early-termination fee equal to X% of remaining committed ARR (commercially negotiable).

2) Operational impacts:
- Billing: Finance needs a clear invoice adjustment flow. Pro rata credits are straightforward if billing is monthly; for prepaid multi-month invoices we require a memo and credit note process (3–5 business days).
- Data export/assistance: Engineering/Support provides a standard export and 20 hours of transition assistance (remote), beyond which time & materials rates apply.
- SLA for handoffs: CSM assigns an offboarding owner within 5 business days of notice.

3) Timing scenarios (playbook excerpt):
- 60-day notice: standard handoff, CSM-led offboarding, finance credit processed in 1 invoice cycle.
- 30-day notice + fee: accelerated project plan, potential partial forfeiture of prepaid discounts, finance processes early-term fee.
- Immediate termination for cause: separate; preserves refunds only per cause clause.

4) Recommended redline: Itrack the clause with the optional 30-day/fee path and a defined calculation for the fee (e.g., 25% of remaining committed ARR) so procurement can run numbers.

Next steps: Amelia — if Acme is ok with receiving the tracked redline + playbook, we'll send both and Karina (our finance lead) can run a sample math for your deal to show the delta between 30 vs 60 day scenarios.

Adding commercial/ops perspective for modeling:

Quick bullets for procurement to consider (I kept this short so they can paste into a vendor-comparison matrix):
- 60-day no-fee T4C: typical, nicer for customers, limited refund risk when billing monthly. For prepaid annual deals, pro rata refunds are possible but reduce recognition; worse for Redwood economics if they take a big discount up front.
- 30-day with early-termination fee: reduces churn risk and protects negotiated discount. We usually model the fee as 20–30% of remaining committed ARR depending on discount depth.
- Data & support: standard 20 hrs included; anything beyond is T&M at $250/hr.
- Admin lead times: finance credit notes take one invoice cycle (up to 30 days); engineering exports require 3 business days for standard data sets.

Action items:
1) Karthik: please send the tracked redline + playbook to Amelia (per your note).
2) Jonas: can you ask Karina (finance) to run a quick sample calc for DEAL-7831 showing the delta between 60-day no fee vs 30-day + 25% fee? Procurement will want a table.
3) Amelia: confirm whether Acme prefers the optional 30-day/fee path or wants the standard 60-day.

Amelia —

Summary paragraph (for your vendor matrix):
Redwood offers a standard 60-day Termination for Convenience (T4C) with pro rata credit for unused prepaid term and 20 hours of transition assistance included. As a commercial concession, Redwood can support a 30-day T4C if the customer accepts an early-termination fee (example: 25% of remaining committed ARR) to protect discounts provided for multi-year commitments. Finance processes pro rata credits via a credit note within one invoice cycle; engineering delivers standard data exports within 3 business days and CSM assigns an offboarding owner within 5 business days.

Example calc for DEAL-7831 (illustrative):
- Remaining committed ARR: $120,000
- 30-day early-termination fee @25% = $30,000
- Pro rata unused prepaid (if customer prepaid 6 months): refundable portion = $15,000 (processed as credit note)
- Net impact to customer in example = $15,000 net payment (fee minus refund)

Next steps: Karthik will send the tracked redline and the playbook to you after this note; Karina will send the sample spreadsheet for DEAL-7831 by EOD. If you confirm preference for 30-day + fee, Marissa and I will prepare the exact language to insert in the order form.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
